Eureka! This setup is called "monoblade", well at least by BMW. The linkage driving the wiper is not a simple cranked pivot at the center of the windshield. The likage is much more complex and produces a sweeping motion across the center of the glass and two arcs at the edges. This is an ingenious solution, but it has some downsides. The first downside is the amount of time needed for a single blade to cover the whole windshield is lengthier than a two-blade setup which results in less water clearing ability during heavy downpours. The second is the increased complexity of the linkage means more points of failure and higher part replacement costs. Overall it's a cool design but likely does little to offset the cost on wiper blades in the long term.
